questions.q: What was the sign outside Long John Silver's tavern?
choices: A large brass telescope
A big ship's anchor made of iron
A painted green parrot
A wooden leg
questions.evidence: a little tavern with a large brass telescope for sign

questions.q: How did Long John Silver get around?
choices: On a crutch, hopping like a bird
In a chair with wheels pushed by a boy
On a wooden leg with a cane
Carried about by his men
questions.evidence: hopping about upon it like a bird

questions.q: Why did Jim stop worrying that Silver was the one-legged sailor he had watched for?
choices: Silver seemed clean and pleasant, not like the pirates Jim had met
Silver showed Jim papers proving he had never been to sea
The squire told Jim that Silver was a different man
Silver said he had lost his leg only a month before

questions.q: What small reaction from Silver hints that he knew more than he said when he saw the squire's letter?
choices: He gave something almost like a start
He tore the letter up into pieces
He went pale and had to sit down on a bench
He refused to read it
questions.evidence: he seemed to me to give something almost like a start

questions.q: Whom did Jim recognize hurrying out of the tavern?
choices: Black Dog
Blind Pew
Mr. Dance
Tom Redruth

questions.q: What reason did Silver first give for sending Harry after the man?
choices: He hadn't paid his score
He had stolen Silver's crutch
He was a wanted pirate
He owed Silver a favor
questions.evidence: But he hasn't paid his score.

questions.q: What did Tom Morgan say he and Black Dog had been talking about?
choices: Keel-hauling
Treasure maps
The squire's new ship
The weather

questions.q: Jim says Silver's show of excitement "would have convinced an Old Bailey judge." What does this tell us?
choices: Silver's act was so good it could fool an expert at spotting lies
Silver had once worked as a judge in the courts of London
Silver was about to be arrested and taken to court
Silver wanted to bring Black Dog before a judge
questions.evidence: such a show of excitement as would have convinced an Old Bailey judge

questions.q: How did Jim feel about Silver by the time the runners came back without Black Dog?
choices: He was convinced Silver was innocent
He was sure Silver was a pirate
He was very afraid of Silver
He was angry with Silver for lying to the squire
questions.evidence: I would have gone bail for the innocence of Long John Silver

questions.q: What made Silver suddenly burst out laughing until tears ran down his cheeks?
choices: He remembered Black Dog left without paying for his rum
Jim told him a funny story about the old captain
Morgan fell off his bench and spilled his drink
Harry came back into the tavern dragging Black Dog by the collar

questions.q: What did Silver do on the walk along the quays that made Jim like him?
choices: Told him about the ships and taught him sea phrases
Bought him a new hat and coat for the voyage
Showed him a treasure map he kept in his apron
Let him steer a small boat across the harbour
questions.evidence: telling me about the different ships that we passed by

questions.q: Why might Silver have told the squire the story of Black Dog "with the most perfect truth"?
choices: To earn the gentlemen's trust
Because Jim forced him to tell it
Because he did not know how to lie
To get Black Dog arrested quickly
questions.evidence: with a great deal of spirit and the most perfect truth

questions.q: What did Dr. Livesey say about Silver after he left?
choices: "John Silver suits me."
"I do not trust that man."
"He is too old to sail."
"He should be captain."
